sections.html: Large (10-12 cm) Lebiasina tetras imported from Colombia for the first time. The species identification is not completely certain; the animals come closest to L. multimaculatus, so "cf." (confer, compare with) is placed between genus and species name.

These fish are incredibly incompatible with each other. With their impressive teeth they cause heavy damage very fast in case of conflicts. They are also incredibly voracious. Because of these characteristics they are only suitable for specialists in predatory fish.

The animals originate from the Choco region in the south of Colombia, from where the emperor tetras Nematobrycon lacortei and N. palmeri are also exported regularly; young Lebiasina are found between them from time to time. Seven Lebiasina species occur in the Choco region: L. astrigata, L. aureoguttata, L. chocoensis, L. festae, L. narinensi and L. multimaculatus. Of these, L. astrigata, L. chocoensis, L. narinensi and L. multimaculatus have a similar color pattern.
The fish are greedily searching for food; within 30 seconds of release they were looking for the remains of a food tablet. A large batch of Tubifex distracted them.

The animals are incredibly incompatible with each other, and the photo session could only be carried out under greatest precautions with a pair. Part of the incompatibility may be due to them trying to eat each other. The more dominant male ate the Tubifex immediately and then largely left the somewhat shyer female alone. The animals are obligatory air breathers.
The sexes can be easily distinguished by the anal fin, which is much larger in sexually mature males than in females of comparable size.
Nothing is known about possible brood care in Lebiasina. Systematically they are relatives of the pencil fish (Nannostomus and Co.), in which males also have an enlarged anal fin.
